questions.question: What does the fact that Rembrandt's mother was Catholic and his father belonged to the Dutch Reformed Church most directly suggest about his personal circumstances?
options: He grew up in a household with mixed religious affiliations, which may have contributed to his deep engagement with religious themes.
He was raised exclusively in the Dutch Reformed tradition, with no exposure to Catholicism.
His parents' religious differences caused him to reject organized religion entirely.
His family's religious background had no influence on his artistic subject matter.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that his mother was Catholic and his father belonged to the Dutch Reformed Church, and that 'Religion is a central theme in Rembrandt's works', implying that this mixed religious upbringing likely influenced his art.
Incorrect. The article explicitly says his mother was Catholic, so he was not raised exclusively in the Dutch Reformed tradition.
Incorrect. The article does not suggest he rejected organized religion; rather, religion remained a central theme in his works.
Incorrect. The article directly links his religious background to the central theme of religion in his art, so it did have influence.

questions.question: Why did Rembrandt not marry Hendrickje Stoffels, even though they had a long-term relationship and a daughter?
options: Because marrying her would have caused him to lose access to a trust set up for Titus in Saskia's will.
Because he was still legally married to Saskia at the time.
Because Hendrickje refused to marry him due to her religious convictions.
Because the church prohibited him from remarrying after Saskia's death.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states, 'Had he remarried he would have lost access to a trust set up for Titus in Saskia's will.' This explains the financial motivation for not marrying Hendrickje.
Incorrect. Saskia died in 1642, so Rembrandt was a widower and free to remarry legally.
Incorrect. The article does not mention Hendrickje refusing to marry; it focuses on Rembrandt's financial considerations.
Incorrect. The article does not mention any church prohibition on remarriage; instead, it highlights the trust issue.

questions.question: What does the creation of a dummy corporation by Hendrickje and Titus in 1660 most clearly imply about Rembrandt's situation?
options: It was a way to allow Rembrandt to continue selling his art despite his insolvency, by using others as fronts.
It was a way to hide Rembrandt's wealth from his creditors so he could avoid paying debts.
It was a way to transfer ownership of Rembrandt's paintings to his son to prevent them from being sold.
It was a way to legally separate Rembrandt's personal finances from his artistic career.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says they established a 'dummy corporation as art dealers, allowing Rembrandt, who had board and lodging, to continue his artistic pursuits.' This implies it was a front to keep him working despite his insolvency.
Incorrect. The purpose was to let him continue his artistic work, not to hide wealth; his assets had already been surrendered.
Incorrect. The corporation was for art dealing, not specifically to protect paintings from sale.
Incorrect. The corporation was a practical arrangement to keep him working, not a legal separation of finances.

questions.question: How does the article suggest that Rembrandt's financial troubles were related to his personal collecting habits?
options: His penchant for acquiring art, prints, and rare items led him to live beyond his means.
His financial troubles were caused by his lavish spending on houses and parties.
His collecting habits were profitable and helped him pay off his mortgage.
His financial troubles were due to his lack of success as a painter.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states, 'His penchant for acquiring art, prints, and rare items led him to live beyond his means.' This directly links his collecting to his financial problems.
Incorrect. The article mentions his collecting habits, not spending on houses and parties, as the cause.
Incorrect. The article indicates his collection did not yield expected returns, as sale prices were disappointing.
Incorrect. Rembrandt was artistically successful; his troubles were financial, not due to lack of success.

questions.question: What does the rejection of 'The Conspiracy of Claudius Civilis' by the mayors suggest about the relationship between Rembrandt and his patrons?
options: Even major commissions could be rejected, indicating that Rembrandt's artistic choices did not always align with the expectations of influential clients.
Rembrandt's work was always accepted without question by his patrons.
The rejection was due to the painting being too small for the town hall.
The mayors rejected the painting because Rembrandt was bankrupt and they did not want to pay him.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the work was 'rejected by the mayors and returned to the painter within a few weeks', showing that even a major project could fail to satisfy patrons.
Incorrect. The rejection of this major project contradicts the idea that his work was always accepted.
Incorrect. The article says the surviving fragment is only a quarter of the original, but does not say the size was the reason for rejection.
Incorrect. The article does not link the rejection to his bankruptcy; it implies artistic reasons.

questions.question: Why did Rembrandt's students copy his self-portraits, and what does this imply about the authenticity of some works attributed to him?
options: It was part of their training, which means that some self-portraits attributed to Rembrandt may actually be by his students.
It was to create forgeries to sell, which explains why so many self-portraits exist.
It was to honor Rembrandt, but it does not affect the attribution of his works.
It was because Rembrandt refused to paint self-portraits himself, so students had to do it for him.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says 'he had his students copy his own self-portraits as part of their training' and that modern scholarship has reduced the autograph count, implying some works once attributed to him are now known to be student copies.
Incorrect. The purpose was training, not forgery, and the article does not suggest they were sold as originals.
Incorrect. The article directly links the copies to the reduction in the autograph count, so it does affect attribution.
Incorrect. Rembrandt painted many self-portraits himself; the copies were in addition to his own work.

questions.question: What does the fluctuation in the number of paintings attributed to Rembrandt over time most clearly demonstrate?
options: The attribution of old master works is not fixed and can change significantly with new scholarship.
Rembrandt's actual output varied greatly depending on the period of his life.
Connoisseurs in the 19th century were more accurate than modern scholars.
Rembrandt's paintings were often lost or destroyed, reducing the count over time.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article shows that the number went from over 600 in the early 20th century to nearer 300 today due to the Rembrandt Research Project, demonstrating that scholarship can winnow attributions.
Incorrect. The fluctuation is due to attribution changes, not changes in his actual output.
Incorrect. The article suggests modern scholarship is more rigorous, as it has reduced the count.
Incorrect. The article does not mention loss or destruction; it focuses on reattribution.

questions.question: What does the fact that Rembrandt was allowed to retain his tools after his bankruptcy imply about the authorities' view of his situation?
options: They saw his artistic ability as a means for him to generate income and pay off his debts.
They were indifferent to his financial problems and allowed him to keep tools as a formality.
They wanted to punish him by allowing him to work but not profit from it.
They believed his tools were worthless and not worth selling.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states he was 'permitted to retain his tools as a means of generating income', showing that the authorities saw his art as a way to repay debts.
Incorrect. The permission was purposeful, not a formality, as it was explicitly to generate income.
Incorrect. The article does not suggest punishment; it suggests leniency and practical support.
Incorrect. The tools were valuable enough to be a means of income, so they were not considered worthless.

questions.question: How does the article's description of Rembrandt's self-portraits as an 'intimate autobiography' relate to the fact that he painted over 40 of them?
options: The large number of self-portraits over his lifetime allows viewers to trace his personal and artistic development, making them a visual record of his life.
The self-portraits are all identical, showing that he was not interested in documenting change.
The self-portraits were primarily for sale to collectors, not for personal expression.
The self-portraits were all painted in his youth, so they do not reflect his later life.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says his oil paintings 'trace the progress from an uncertain young man, through the dapper and very successful portrait-painter of the 1630s, to the troubled but massively powerful portraits of his old age', which supports the idea of an intimate autobiography.
Incorrect. The article describes a progression, not identical works.
Incorrect. The article does not mention selling self-portraits; it emphasizes their autobiographical nature.
Incorrect. The article mentions self-portraits from his old age, so they span his lifetime.

questions.question: What does the fact that Rembrandt was influenced by Italian Old Masters and Dutch/Flemish artists who had studied in Italy, despite never going abroad himself, suggest about artistic influence in the 17th century?
options: Artists could be significantly influenced by foreign styles through the works and knowledge of other artists who had traveled.
Artists had to travel to Italy to be influenced by Italian masters, as there was no other way.
Italian influence was not possible without direct contact with Italian artists.
Rembrandt's lack of travel meant he was completely isolated from foreign artistic trends.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states he was 'considerably influenced by the work of the Italian Old Masters and Dutch and Flemish artists who had studied in Italy', showing that influence could be transmitted indirectly.
Incorrect. Rembrandt never went abroad yet was influenced, so travel was not necessary.
Incorrect. The article shows influence occurred through other artists' exposure, not direct contact.
Incorrect. The article explicitly says he was influenced, so he was not isolated.
